name: Responding to Hostility and Anger in Public Witness
description: Videos where abolitionists face angry, profane, or aggressive opposition in public spaces and respond calmly with the gospel, free speech, and the case that abortion is murder. The video must show how to handle hostility, ad hominem attacks, or demands to leave.
titles: "You Got Me FIRED!!" Crazy Professor Wants Revenge
They don't need to know that!

name: Street Conversations: Answering Objections to Abortion Abolition and the Bible
description: The video must show a live street conversation in which an abolitionist answers a skeptic's objection to the abolitionist position or to Christianity, such as bodily autonomy, abortion as healthcare, slavery history, or biblical authority, and ties the answer back to the humanity of the preborn.
titles: Condescending Woman Tries to Run Me Out of Town
College Student Actually Listens when Corrected by Historian
College Kid Fails to Follow Basic Reasoning
The church fathers aren't with you
Am I Talking to a Fake Christian?
We live in a first-world country

name: Answering Bodily Autonomy and "My Body, My Choice" on the Street
description: Street conversations where the abolitionist responds to the bodily autonomy objection, showing that the preborn child is a distinct human with their own body and that autonomy or duty-to-rescue arguments do not justify intentionally killing them.
titles: What can I take away from you?
Pro-Choicer Actually Listens After Running Out of Arguments
"SCIENCE" is NOT on the Side of Abortion
The ulterior motives of a white knight

name: Deflections and "What About..." Objections: Staying Focused on Abortion
description: Street conversations where a passerby deflects from abortion by pointing to other issues (born children's needs, foster care, adoption, war, Gaza, BLM, ad hominem attacks) and the abolitionist answers by keeping the focus on the preborn child's equal right to life and protection.
titles: “I Would Murder My Child to Protect Them from Abuse”

name: Street Conversations: Proving the Preborn Are Living Humans
description: Videos where an abolitionist answers objections denying the preborn child is alive or human, using biology, embryology, and logical consistency (e.g., parasite, heartbeat, birth-as-threshold, fetal development claims).
titles: "Stop Mansplaining!!" Abortion Loving Students Can't Handle Debate
Pro-Abortion Girl Caught LYING! Loses Debate

name: Public Witness Pushback: Free Speech, Officials, and Graphic Signs
description: Videos where abolitionists doing public outreach with graphic abortion imagery face objections or interference, either from officials, police, or security citing rules and permits, or from passersby offended by the signs, and respond by defending their free speech rights and the necessity of the imagery.
titles: We "Officially" Got Kicked Out of the Medieval Fair
I'm with the University, and I'm here to help.
Bad Cops VS. Abortion Abolitionists “No! You Cannot Arrest Me!”
Catholic School Debate Teacher Defends Abortion

name: Street Conversations: Answering Hostile and Dismissive Pushback
description: Videos of live street conversations in which an abolitionist defends equal protection for the preborn against objections, insults, and dismissals (slavery and Nazi comparisons, personhood assertions, Sharia and religious-imposition charges, bodily autonomy). The video should show how to stay composed and return to the argument.
titles: Pro-Aborts ATTACK When They Can't Debate
Pro-Choicers Openly Admit They Don't Believe in "Human Rights"
Cocky Woman Gives Up After Her Arguments Crumble
Pro-Choicer Tries to LIE About Me to My FACE
Should the strong protect the weak?

name: Why Human Life Has Value: Answering Human Rights Objections
description: Street conversations where the abolitionist defends the inherent, objective value of every human being, often grounded in the image of God, against objections that tie human worth to cognitive ability, sentience, utility, species equivalence, overpopulation, or moral relativism.
titles: You don't believe in human rights

name: Handling Pushback Over Sidewalks, Permits, and Police
description: Videos where abolitionists face business owners, vendors, event organizers, rival groups, or police over their right to do street outreach on public property, showing how to respond calmly, know legal boundaries, and decide when to stay or move.
titles: I Got Punched in the Face...
ICE Agent Tries To Deport Us
We Got BANNED from the "Freedom" Trail

name: Street Conversations: Confronting Abortion and Calling for Repentance
description: Videos of live street conversations where an abolitionist answers objections to abortion, from hostility and mockery to post-abortive guilt, calls it murder of a human image-bearer, and points people to repentance and the Gospel.
titles: Telling People Who've Had Abortions the Truth
"Can I Slap You?" Pro-Choicers Get Mad
“Men are Pigs!” Women HAVE to Abort Babies!
I Told a Trans Activist that She's Not Oppressed
The Gospel for Women After Abortion

name: Abolition vs. Incrementalism: Slavery Parallels and Public Witness
description: Videos that argue for immediate abolition of abortion over incremental or compromise strategies, often by drawing on the history of slavery abolitionism, and that show this message in street outreach, debates, or teaching. A video belongs if it defends immediatism, calls out compromise or the status quo of legal abortion, or compares abortion to slavery.
titles: Boston Pro-Choicers Confronted by Hundreds of Abolitionists
Does the Pro-Life Movement Hate Justice?
Abolitionism vs. Incrementalism DEBATE w/ Doug Wilson
What No One Else Will Tell You About Lincoln or Trump

name: Handling Hecklers, Deflection, and Refusals on the Street
description: Videos where a street conversation is derailed by mockery, insults, jokes, silence, or refusal to engage, and the abolitionist responds by staying calm, naming the deflection, or redirecting to the issue of abortion.
titles: It won't go well for you!
I don't know what that means

name: Responding to Objections About Filming Street Outreach
description: Videos where abolitionists answer objections to being filmed while doing public outreach, such as claims of creepiness, lack of consent, privacy violations, or deceit, and show how to defend the right to film calmly and steer back to the gospel and abortion.
titles: Pro-Life Leader Threatens to Sue Us

name: Street Conversations: Answering 'My Body, My Choice' and Personal-Hardship Excuses
description: Videos of street conversations where an abolitionist answers objections that justify abortion by appeal to bodily autonomy, selfishness, financial or career hardship, personal trauma, or 'who will help' deflections, by affirming the preborn child's humanity and calling abortion child sacrifice or murder.
titles: Proud Atheist Confused When Christian Agrees With Him

name: Justice, Capital Punishment, and the Role of Civil Government
description: Videos where the abolitionist applies biblical justice to explain why civil government must punish evil, including capital punishment for capital crimes, the difference between murder and just execution, and why the innocent preborn must be protected. Also includes cases of restitution, accountability, and defending others.
titles: Didn't go the way he wanted...

name: "Men Can't Talk About Abortion": Answering Gender-Based Objections
description: Videos where an abolitionist responds to the objection that men (or white men, or non-pregnant people) have no right to speak on abortion, by showing that protecting human life is not gender-specific and drawing on historical abolition parallels.
titles: Irate Woman: No Man Can Tell Me Not To Murder!
“You’re a White Man!” You can’t talk about that!
Don't tell a white man he can't fly

name: Worldview Challenges: Science, God, and Objective Truth
description: Street conversations where the abolitionist confronts foundational worldview claims (science as moral authority, evolution, relativism, God as the standard of morality) rather than only abortion-specific arguments, grounding the discussion in objective truth and human rights.
titles: "You're Being Fools!" Pro-Choice Student Embarrassed by His Side
No shelves to put things on
